reputation.summary: ADI's AN-1429 lists the ADA4627-1 with the AD797, OP275 and AD8620 as op-amps 'reputable with music fans' (vendor marketing). A diyAudio thread, 'ADA4627 outperforms Burr-Brown's OPA627', calls it refined and dynamic; a Japanese Dr.DAC3 comparison (Shirokuma) heard less treble harshness than the OPA627. The ADA4637-1 is liked for DAC I/V. No independent measurements found.
typical_uses: OPA627 alternative in single sockets (SOIC-to-DIP adapter)
DAC I/V (ADA4637-1 only at noise gain ≥ 5)
op-amp rolling in DACs and headphone gear (Dr.DAC3)
caveats: ADA4637-1 needs noise gain ≥ 5; not for unity-gain buffers or low-gain stages.
Single only, SOIC-8 or LFCSP-8, no DIP; dual sockets need an adapter.
Slew advantage over OPA627 (55 V/µs) is marginal for ADA4627-1, clear for ADA4637-1.
Sonic claims are subjective forum and blog listening; AN-1429 praise is marketing.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports found. Claims that fans prefer it because, unlike the OPA627, it is not faked are low-confidence folklore. Buy from ADI or authorised distributors; avoid marketplace 'ADA4627 on DIP adapter' modules of unknown provenance.

silicon_changes.identification: Laser-marked pin-1 indicator after the change; country of origin and date code separate assembly sites. Not verified per part.
silicon_changes.summary: Amkor Philippines qualified to assemble 3×3 mm LFCSP products, sawn-singulated leadframe, Amkor standard BOM, laser-marked pin 1. Assembly only, no die change. ADA4627-1/ADA4637-1 inclusion unconfirmed; would affect LFCSP only, not SOIC ARZ/BRZ.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None expected: same die, package assembly only.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: assembly-only, and only the LFCSP, rarely used for rolling.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN content confirmed; ADA4627-1/ADA4637-1 not confirmed on its parts list.
